concepts.title: OSI Model, TCP/IP Model และการสำรวจ Interface ของเครื่อง (ip, ipconfig)
concepts.covers: Explain the 7 OSI layers and 4 TCP/IP layers with PDU names (Bits, Frame, Packet, Segment/Datagram, Data), encapsulation/decapsulation, and where common protocols/devices sit (Hub L1, Switch L2, Router L3, Firewall L3-L7). Mnemonic for the layer order. CODE EXAMPLE: (1) runnable Python file `osi_layers.py` (standard library only) that prints a deterministic table of the 7 layers with PDU and example protocols, then simulates encapsulation of the string 'GET /' by wrapping it in fake [TCP sport=50000 dport=80], [IP 192.168.1.37->192.0.2.10], [ETH ...] headers and prints each step, then decapsulates; (2) wsl block `ip -br link`, `ip -br addr`, `ip -4 addr show eth0` with realistic WSL NAT-mode output (eth0 172.24.85.123/20, say values differ); (3) win block `ipconfig /all` excerpt and `Get-NetIPAddress -AddressFamily IPv4` (not runnable here; realistic, say values differ). Mistakes: mixing up layer numbers, `ifconfig: command not found` (net-tools not installed; use ip), reading the Windows IP instead of the WSL IP.

concepts.title: Ethernet, MAC Address และ ARP (ip link, ip neigh, Network Namespace)
concepts.covers: Ethernet frame fields (dst MAC, src MAC, EtherType, payload, FCS), MAC format and OUI, unicast/broadcast ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff, how a switch learns its MAC table, ARP request/reply and the ARP cache, Wi-Fi basics recap (2.4/5/6 GHz, SSID, WPA2/WPA3). CODE EXAMPLE (runnable with sudo): build two Linux network namespaces `pc1` and `pc2` joined by a veth pair with FIXED MAC addresses 02:00:00:00:00:01 and 02:00:00:00:00:02 and IPs 192.168.50.1/24 and 192.168.50.2/24; `ip netns exec pc1 ping -c 2 192.168.50.2`; show `ip netns exec pc1 ip neigh` (REACHABLE entry with the fixed MAC); optionally `tcpdump -i` inside the namespace with `-e -c 4 arp or icmp` to show the ARP who-has/is-at lines; cleanup with `ip netns del`. Windows: `arp -a` (realistic). Mistakes: `Cannot open network namespace "pc1": No such file or directory`, forgetting `ip link set ... up` (ping gives `Network is unreachable` or 100% loss), `RTNETLINK answers: File exists` on rerun (delete first).

concepts.title: IPv4 Addressing, Subnetting และ CIDR ด้วยมือและด้วย Python ipaddress
concepts.covers: Binary/decimal conversion, network/host portion, subnet mask vs prefix length, network address, broadcast, usable hosts (2^h - 2), /31 and /32 special cases, private ranges RFC 1918, 127.0.0.0/8, 169.254.0.0/16 APIPA, 100.64.0.0/10 CGNAT, documentation ranges. Worked examples: 192.168.1.0/24 into 4 x /26, 10.10.0.0/16 into /20s, finding the subnet of 172.16.45.200/21, VLSM for 4 departments (60, 28, 12, 2 hosts) from 192.168.100.0/24. CODE EXAMPLE: `subnet_calc.py` (standard library ipaddress) that takes a CIDR via argparse (default 192.168.1.0/24) and an optional --new-prefix, prints network, netmask, wildcard, broadcast, first/last host, host count, is_private, and lists child subnets; run with `python3 subnet_calc.py 192.168.1.0/24 --new-prefix 26`; real output. This file is reused as hnt/subnet.py in the Mini Project. Mistakes: `ValueError: 192.168.1.10/24 has host bits set` (use strict=False or the network address), forgetting -2 for usable hosts, confusing wildcard 0.0.0.63 with mask.

concepts.title: IPv6 พื้นฐาน และ DHCP (DORA)
concepts.covers: IPv6 128-bit format, hex groups, shortening rules (leading zeros, one :: only), prefix /64, address types (global unicast 2000::/3, link-local fe80::/10, unique local fc00::/7, multicast ff00::/8, loopback ::1), documentation prefix 2001:db8::/32, SLAAC and EUI-64 concept, NDP replacing ARP. DHCP: DORA (Discover, Offer, Request, Ack) on UDP 67/68, lease time, options (router, DNS), DHCP relay concept, APIPA 169.254.x.x when DHCP fails. CODE EXAMPLE: `ipv6_tool.py` using ipaddress: compress/expand 2001:0db8:0000:0000:0000:ff00:0042:8329, classify several addresses (is_link_local, is_global, is_private, is_multicast), split 2001:db8:abcd::/48 into the first 4 /64 subnets, compute an EUI-64 link-local from MAC 02:00:00:00:00:01 (flip the U/L bit, insert ff:fe); real output. Plus `ip -6 addr` (realistic) and Windows `ipconfig /release` / `ipconfig /renew` explanation (not runnable; describe effect). Mistakes: using :: twice (`ValueError: At most one '::' permitted`), forgetting brackets in URLs (`http://[::1]:8000/`), DHCP gives 169.254.x.x.

concepts.title: DNS: Record, การ Resolve, dig และ socket.getaddrinfo
concepts.covers: Resolution chain (stub resolver, recursive resolver, root, TLD, authoritative), caching and TTL, record types A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, NS, PTR, SOA, SRV, /etc/hosts and /etc/resolv.conf in WSL (generated by WSL; `generateResolvConf` in /etc/wsl.conf), split-horizon concept, home.arpa reserved for home networks. CODE EXAMPLE: reuse the Part 1 local DNS lab exactly: dnsmasq on 127.0.0.1 port 5300 with --local=/home.arpa/, host-records router.home.arpa 192.168.1.1, nas.home.arpa 192.168.1.20, mail.home.arpa 192.168.1.25, CNAME files.home.arpa -> nas.home.arpa, MX home.arpa -> mail.home.arpa 10, TXT 'v=spf1 mx -all', local-ttl 300; query with `dig @127.0.0.1 -p 5300` (+short, +noall +answer, -x, NXDOMAIN). Then `dns_lookup.py` that uses socket.getaddrinfo to resolve 'localhost' (127.0.0.1 and ::1), socket.gethostbyaddr('127.0.0.1') for the reverse name, and shows the error-handling path for 'printer.home.arpa' (catch socket.gaierror and print a Thai message). Do not edit /etc/hosts. Real output. Mistakes: `connection timed out; no servers could be reached`, `dnsmasq: failed to create listening socket for port 53: Permission denied` (use 5300), stale cache/TTL, editing /etc/resolv.conf that WSL overwrites.

concepts.title: TCP, UDP และ Port: เขียน Server/Client ด้วย Python socket แล้วดูด้วย ss และ tcpdump
concepts.covers: TCP vs UDP, ports and well-known numbers, sockets and the 5-tuple, 3-way handshake, FIN/RST, TCP states (LISTEN, ESTABLISHED, TIME-WAIT), Connection refused vs timed out, ephemeral ports. CODE EXAMPLE: `tcp_echo_server.py` (binds 127.0.0.1:9000, echoes upper-cased text, handles one client per loop) and `tcp_echo_client.py` (sends 'hello network'), plus `udp_echo.py` (server and client in one file using threading on 127.0.0.1:9001); run in two terminals; show `ss -tlnp | grep 9000` and `ss -ulnp | grep 9001`; `sudo tcpdump -i lo -nn -c 6 'tcp port 9000'` to see SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK, data, FIN; and `nc -zv 127.0.0.1 9000` / 9002 (refused). Real output; say ports/seq/time differ. Mistakes: `OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use` (use SO_REUSEADDR or wait), `ConnectionRefusedError: [Errno 111] Connection refused`, forgetting encode()/decode() (`TypeError: a bytes-like object is required, not 'str'`).

concepts.title: HTTP, HTTPS และ TLS: curl -v, openssl และ HTTPS Server ใน Lab
concepts.covers:
HTTP request/response anatomy, methods, status codes, headers, HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2 vs HTTP/3 (QUIC over UDP 443), TLS goals, TLS 1.3 handshake summary, certificates, SAN, chain of trust, SNI. CODE EXAMPLE: in ~/projects/network-lab/tls-lab create a self-signed certificate for localhost with `openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -keyout key.pem -out cert.pem -days 30 -subj '/CN=localhost' -addext 'subjectAltName=DNS:localhost,IP:127.0.0.1'`; `https_server.py` using http.server + ssl.SSLContext(PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER) on 127.0.0.1:8443 serving index.html ('

Hello TLS

'); then `curl -sv --cacert cert.pem https://localhost:8443/ -o /dev/null` (show TLSv1.3 lines, subject, SAN match, HTTP/1.0 200), `curl https://localhost:8443/` without --cacert to show `curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: self-signed certificate`, and `openssl s_client -connect localhost:8443 -servername localhost

concepts.title: Routing, Default Gateway และ NAT ด้วย Linux Network Namespace
concepts.covers: Routing table fields, longest prefix match, connected/static/default routes, ip_forward, TTL and traceroute, NAT/PAT translation table, RFC 1918, WSL2 NAT mode vs mirrored mode (.wslconfig networkingMode=mirrored, Windows 11 22H2+, trade-offs) as in Part 1 Step 8. CODE EXAMPLE (runnable with sudo; script file `routing_lab.sh` with set -e and a cleanup at start): namespaces `lan1` (10.0.1.10/24, gw 10.0.1.1), `router` (10.0.1.1/24 and 10.0.2.1/24, net.ipv4.ip_forward=1) and `lan2` (10.0.2.20/24, gw 10.0.2.1) via veth pairs; show `ip netns exec lan1 ip route`, `ip netns exec lan1 ip route get 10.0.2.20`, ping across, `ip netns exec lan1 tracepath -n 10.0.2.20` (2 hops), then delete the default route in lan2 to show the failure and restore it; add a NAT section: in `router` run `iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s 10.0.1.0/24 -o r-lan2 -j MASQUERADE` and show with tcpdump in lan2 that the source becomes 10.0.2.1; cleanup script. Real output. Also Packet Tracer static-route config matching Part 1 (R1 192.168.10.1/24, R1-R2 link 10.0.12.0/30, R2 LAN 192.168.20.0/24) in a Cisco IOS block. Mistakes: forgetting ip_forward (ping 100% loss), missing return route, `RTNETLINK answers: Network is unreachable` when adding a gateway outside the connected subnet.

concepts.title: VLAN, 802.1Q Trunk, Inter-VLAN Routing และ STP
concepts.covers: VLAN purpose, access vs trunk, 802.1Q tag (4 bytes, 12-bit VID 1-4094), native VLAN, router-on-a-stick vs SVI, broadcast storm, STP/RSTP root election, port roles, PortFast + BPDU Guard. CODE EXAMPLES: (1) Cisco IOS (data-env app, label 'Cisco IOS · Packet Tracer', language-plaintext, '!' comments in Thai) for SW1 2960: vlan 10 SALES, vlan 20 HR, Fa0/1 access 10, Fa0/2 access 20, Gi0/1 trunk allowed 10,20; R1 Gi0/0.10 and Gi0/0.20 with encapsulation dot1Q and 192.168.10.1/24, 192.168.20.1/24; show vlan brief / show interfaces trunk sample output written to IOS format (state it is example output from Packet Tracer). (2) Runnable Linux equivalent: namespaces `sw-host1`, `sw-host2` and `rtr` where rtr has a veth with 802.1Q sub-interfaces `ip link add link r-trunk name r-trunk.10 type vlan id 10` and `.20`; hosts in VLAN 10 (192.168.10.10) and VLAN 20 (192.168.20.10) on tagged sub-interfaces; ping across through rtr; `sudo tcpdump -e -nn -i <trunk veth> -c 4` shows 'ethertype 802.1Q (0x8100), length ..: vlan 10'. Real output. Mistakes: VLAN not allowed on trunk, native VLAN mismatch (%CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH), 3560 needing `switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q`, err-disabled port after BPDU Guard.

concepts.title: Dynamic Routing: OSPF (Cost และ SPF) และแนวคิด BGP
concepts.covers: Static vs dynamic routing, distance vector vs link state, OSPF router-id, hello/dead 10/40, neighbor states, LSAs, area 0, cost = reference bandwidth / interface bandwidth (default 100 Mbps; auto-cost reference-bandwidth 1000), wildcard masks, passive-interface, DR/BDR; BGP concepts (AS, ASN, private ASN 64512-65534, eBGP vs iBGP, TCP 179, AS_PATH, policy-based, route leaks, RPKI), administrative distance table. CODE EXAMPLES: (1) Cisco IOS OSPF on R1, R2, R3 in a triangle (R1 1.1.1.1 LAN 192.168.10.0/24, R2 2.2.2.2 LAN 192.168.20.0/24, R3 3.3.3.3 LAN 192.168.30.0/24; links 10.0.12.0/30, 10.0.13.0/30, 10.0.23.0/30), show ip ospf neighbor / show ip route ospf as Packet Tracer example output. (2) Runnable `ospf_spf.py`: Dijkstra with heapq over the same triangle where R1-R2 is 100 Mbps and the others 1 Gbps, computing cost with reference bandwidth 1000 Mbps (cost 10 vs 1), prints the shortest path and total cost from R1 to every LAN, then simulates the R1-R3 link failing and recomputes; real deterministic output. Mistakes: area mismatch, hello/dead mismatch, duplicate router-id, wrong wildcard (0.0.0.255 vs 255.255.255.0), forgetting to set the same reference bandwidth everywhere.

concepts.title: Firewall, ACL, VPN และการสแกน Port ในระบบของตัวเอง (nftables, nmap)
concepts.covers: Stateless vs stateful, default deny, rule order, zones/DMZ, host firewalls (ufw on servers, Windows Defender Firewall, nftables underneath), Cisco standard/extended/named ACLs, implicit deny, placement rules, VPN types (site-to-site IPsec IKE/ESP, remote access, WireGuard UDP 51820, split vs full tunnel), Zero Trust concept, nmap states open/closed/filtered. SAFETY: scan only 127.0.0.1 and the learner's own namespaces/containers; quote the Thai Computer Crime Act. CODE EXAMPLES: (1) runnable: namespace `srv` (10.0.9.2/24) and `cli` (10.0.9.1/24) via veth; in srv run `python3 -m http.server 8080` and `python3 -m http.server 8081` in the background; `nmap -sT -p 22,8080,8081 10.0.9.2` from cli before rules; then load an nftables ruleset file `srv-firewall.nft` (table inet filter, chain input policy drop, ct state established,related accept, iif lo accept, tcp dport 8080 accept, icmp accept) with `ip netns exec srv nft -f`; rerun nmap to show 8080 open, 8081 filtered, 22 filtered; `nft list ruleset`; cleanup. Real output. (2) Cisco IOS named extended ACL SALES-IN exactly as in Part 1 Step 11 (permit tcp 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 host 192.168.20.10 eq 443; deny ip 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 192.168.20.0 0.0.0.255; permit ip any any; applied in on Gi0/0.10). WireGuard config shown as concept only (do not claim it was run). Mistakes: lockout because established/related missing, rule order, forgetting permit any at the end of an ACL, `nft: command not found` (apt install nftables).

concepts.title: Troubleshooting อย่างเป็นระบบ และ Network Automation ด้วย Python (subprocess, socket, JSON)
concepts.covers: 7-step troubleshooting process, bottom-up/top-down/divide-and-conquer, the standard command ladder (ip addr, ip route, ping 127.0.0.1, ping gateway, ping external, dig, nc/Test-NetConnection, curl -v), documenting incidents, change management, Netmiko/NAPALM/Ansible as next steps (concept only, no install claimed), secrets from environment variables. CODE EXAMPLE: `net_doctor.py` (standard library only: subprocess, socket, ipaddress, json, argparse, datetime, shutil) that runs a checklist and prints PASS/FAIL per layer: default gateway from `ip -j route show default` (JSON), ping -c 1 -W 1 127.0.0.1, DNS resolution of 'localhost' via socket.getaddrinfo, TCP check of 127.0.0.1:<port> (refuses any target outside 127.0.0.0/8 and ::1 with a clear Thai message), writes `net-doctor-report.json`; run once with a local http.server on 8000 running and once without to show FAIL on the port check. Real output; the gateway line differs per machine (say so). Mistakes: `FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'ping'` (install iputils-ping), parsing human-readable output instead of `ip -j`, `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`, ping needing privileges on some systems.

mini_project.name: Home Network Toolkit
mini_project.summary: A portfolio-ready command-line toolkit in pure Python 3.12 (standard library only, no pip packages) for Ubuntu 24.04 in WSL2 that (1) calculates and splits IPv4/IPv6 subnets with ipaddress, (2) looks up DNS names (A/AAAA via socket.getaddrinfo, reverse via gethostbyaddr) and optionally queries a given DNS server with dig through subprocess if dig exists, (3) checks TCP ports ONLY on the learner's own machine (targets restricted to 127.0.0.0/8 and ::1; anything else is refused with a Thai message and exit code 2), (4) writes a dated plain-text network report, and (5) includes a home network diagram. Project root /home/somchai/projects/home-network-toolkit, git repo on branch main, pushed to GitHub.
features: CLI entry point `python3 -m hnt <command>` with argparse subcommands: `subnet CIDR [--new-prefix N]`, `dns NAME [--server IP --port N]`, `ports [--host 127.0.0.1] --ports 22,80,443,5432,8000`, `report [--out reports/]`

Package folder hnt/: __init__.py (version '1.0.0'), __main__.py (argparse), subnet.py (from Concept c03), dnslookup.py (socket + optional dig), portcheck.py (socket.create_connection with timeout 0.5 s, allowlist guard is_allowed_target()), report.py (collects hostname, interfaces from `ip -j -4 addr`, default route from `ip -j route show default`, DNS servers from /etc/resolv.conf, port results; writes reports/network-report-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.txt)
Safety guard: portcheck refuses non-loopback targets; README states the legal rule (พ.ร.บ.ว่าด้วยการกระทำความผิดเกี่ยวกับคอมพิวเตอร์)

Tests with unittest (no pytest needed): tests/test_subnet.py and tests/test_portcheck.py (allowlist logic and a port opened by a temporary socket server in the test), run with `python3 -m unittest -v`

docs/home-network.md containing a Mermaid diagram (GitHub renders it) plus a plaintext ASCII diagram of ISP ONT/router 192.168.1.1, Wi-Fi AP, laptop 192.168.1.37 running WSL (172.24.85.123 behind Windows NAT), NAS 192.168.1.20, printer 192.168.1.50, phone via DHCP; and docs/ip-plan.md table of the home subnet 192.168.1.0/24 with DHCP pool 192.168.1.100-192.168.1.199
README.md (Thai + English headings) with features, usage examples, sample output, safety note, and screenshots-free text; .gitignore ignoring reports/, .venv/, __pycache__/
mini_project.stack: Python 3.12.3 (Ubuntu 24.04 system python3; code must also run on 3.13), standard library only: ipaddress, socket, subprocess, argparse, json, datetime, pathlib, shutil, unittest; optional external CLI tools from apt on Ubuntu 24.04: iproute2 6.1.0, bind9-dnsutils 9.18 (dig), iputils-ping 20240117; Git 2.43.0; GitHub; draw.io optional for a PNG diagram. No venv is strictly needed because there are no pip packages, but mention `python3 -m venv .venv` as the habit for later extensions.
